items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: one of my mentors, Muhal Richard Abrams formed the, oh what was it – the Orchestra — Experimental Orchestra.

ctx.x: Well before you left Chicago, is that when you had an interaction with the members of the AACM? Can you tell me about that?

Well it wasn’t the AACM when I was there. I left the year before the AACM was formed. But the year before that one of my mentors, Muhal Richard Abrams formed the, oh what was it – the Orchestra — Experimental Orchestra. So Roscoe and Joseph Jarman and Malachi Favors, we were all sort of playing in that orchestra, and formed small groups from that orchestra. But then I left the next year and then that’s when Roscoe Mitchell and I think Joseph Jarman, Anthony Braxton I think, yeah. That’s when it was officially…
Was their approach to music startling to you or just something —

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I'd go to Muhal who gave me advice about music, about life and about helping me get over my fear of coming to New York, going to New York.

ctx.x: So you’re just working it out yourself? You didn't have anyone showing you anything?

No, I got a couple of books, Wilcoxon books but I didn't like the books so I got the 26 rudiments and worked through them. Practiced those while I was watching television. I used to practice on all kinds of surfaces because we used to go to the jam sessions in Chicago you had to play sitting in on people's drums which had different tensions on them. Some guys had their drum heads loose, some had them tighter and I found that some guys couldn't play the drums if they weren't a certain tension so I purposely used…
